Subject: Post-call: Throughput sizing & streaming SLOs (Finex)

Hi Alex / Dana  great call today, thanks for walking through the workload. Quick recap and a few open items so we can produce a sizing estimate: 

Recap/high-level requirements:
- Latency SLOs: p95 <= 300ms for single-response flows (typical payload ~512 tokens). For streaming endpoints we need to support chunked delivery with head latency <= 150ms.
- Throughput/shape: you mentioned a steady-state of ~30 QPS and bursts / peak to ~220 QPS during market open. Average tokens per request ~900, with some longer batched jobs hitting ~3k tokens.
- Concurrency: peak concurrent in-flight requests estimated ~140 (average burst) with extreme bursts up to ~400 for a short window.
- Streaming: must support server-sent streaming for partial renders and cancelation support.

Open items for sizing (can you confirm these please):
1) Can you share a 24-72h sample of request timestamps + tokens/request (CSV is fine)?
2) How many simultaneous independent users vs. background batch jobs (percent split)?
3) Any hard constraints on model family (decoder-only vs. chat-style models) or can we recommend quantized variants?

Next steps: please attach the workload CSV (if available) and Ill loop in Marissa and Neha for a preliminary GPU/pool recommendation. Ill follow up with a short note containing tokens/sec, QPS assumptions, and a proposal for an initial Dedicated footprint we can run the pilot on.

Thanks  Rafael
Rafael Mendes

Hi Rafael  thanks for the recap. Confirming the numbers from our side and clarifications below:

Confirmed / clarifications:
- Steady-state: ~30 QPS (during the trading day outside open/close spikes).
- Typical peak: 120 QPS sustained for ~10-15m, plus short bursts up to 220 QPS for ~1-3 minutes during market events.
- Avg tokens/request: 900 (most are 600-1,200), but ~7% of requests are >2,500 tokens.
- Concurrency: during peaks we expect ~120-180 concurrent active requests; worst-case extreme parallelism (rare) could approach 400.
- SLOs: p95 <= 300ms for standard single-response endpoints. For streaming endpoints we need first-byte <= 150ms and steady stream throughput ~15-25 tokens/sec per active connection.

I attached a 72-hour sample export (finex_workload_summary.csv) with timestamps and tokens/request. One more ask: do you have guidance on preferred batching window and max latency tradeoff we should expect from Redwood Dedicated?

Hi Alex  got the CSV, thanks  thats very helpful. I ran a quick pass with Marissa and Neha and heres a conservative preliminary sizing and notes (ballpark for budgeting only):

Assumptions used:
- Model: 13B family (decoder) quantized to 4-bit where acceptable; we prepared estimates for native fp16 as well.
- Avg tokens/request: 900 (as provided).
- Avg generation speed per GPU: ~25 tokens/sec for fp16 on A100-80GB for the config we benchmarked; quantized path can increase tokens/sec by ~1.6x depending on kernel support.
- Streaming: we assumed 18 tokens/sec sustained per active streaming connection for headroom.

Preliminary size (steady vs peak):
- Steady-state (30 QPS): recommend a Dedicated pool of 2 x A100-80GB (fp16) supporting batching + KV cache. Estimated throughput ~1,500-2,000 tokens/sec per GPU => combined ~3,000-4,000 tokens/sec steady. This covers 30 QPS * 900 tokens ~= 27,000 tokens/sec? Note: this mismatch means we need more capacity if all requests are synchronous generation. Given streaming and request concurrency patterns, we recommend using request-level batching + prefix/KV cache to reduce repeated tokens.
- Conservative baseline for synchronous heavy traffic: 6 x A100-80GB to comfortably handle steady-state with room for burst headroom.
- Peak buffer: autoscale up to 8-10 GPUs for short peaks (120-220 QPS) or leverage a mixed pool with cheaper accelerator for scaled bursts.

Tuning levers and tradeoffs:
- Batching window: 10-30ms window recommended for low-latency workloads; larger windows increase tokens/sec throughput but add latency.
- Concurrency per GPU: we recommend limiting simultaneous generation slots to ~8-12 per GPU (depends on sequence length).
- Quantization: 4-bit can drive ~1.4-1.7x improvement in tokens/sec but we should validate quality on your prompts.

Attachments: I attached a short Redwood sizing PDF with two scenarios (cost-optimized vs latency-optimized).

Proposed next step: 30-minute follow-up with Marissa (solutions) + Neha (SRE) to validate assumptions and walk through the CSV traces. Are you available Thu 20th 10:00-10:30 PT or Thu 20th 14:00-14:30 PT?

Cheers,
Rafael
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
